title: Fluid Mechanics / Transport Phenomena I
description: This syllabus treats fluid mechanics as Chemical Engineering's first transport phenomena course: students move from properties and balances to viscous flow, pipe networks, boundary layers, measurement, scale-up, and analogies that prepare them for heat and mass transfer.

topics.title: Transport Phenomena Framework, Continuum Assumptions, and Fluid Properties
topics.description: Frame fluid mechanics as momentum transport and define the physical properties that control flow behavior.

children.title: Momentum Transport as a Unified Framework
children.description: This subtopic positions fluid mechanics as the first piece of a broader transport sequence.

children.title: Momentum flux, momentum diffusivity, molecular transport, and convective transport
Macroscopic balance, microscopic balance, and constitutive relation
Analogies among momentum, heat, and mass transfer
Process examples: pipes, reactors, packed beds, filters, heat exchangers, and columns
Continuum Assumption and Flow Descriptions
children.description: Students learn when it is reasonable to treat a fluid as a continuous field.

children.title: Continuum hypothesis, mean free path, Knudsen number, and representative volume element
Eulerian description, Lagrangian description, streamline, pathline, and streakline
Steady versus unsteady flow, uniform versus nonuniform flow
Compressible versus incompressible flow and low-Mach-number assumption
Fluid Properties and Material Behavior
children.description: The point is to connect measurable properties to flow resistance, interface behavior, and pressure response.

children.title: Density, specific weight, specific gravity, and compressibility
Dynamic viscosity, kinematic viscosity, Newtonian fluid, and apparent viscosity
Surface tension, capillary pressure, wetting, and contact angle
Vapor pressure, cavitation risk, and temperature dependence of properties

topics.title: Fluid Statics, Pressure Variation, and Forces on Surfaces
topics.description: Analyze fluids at rest, hydrostatic pressure fields, buoyancy, and pressure forces.

children.title: Pressure Fields in Static Fluids
children.description: Students learn how pressure changes with depth and body forces.

children.title: Pressure, gauge pressure, absolute pressure, and atmospheric pressure
Hydrostatic equation, pressure gradient, and constant-density fluid
Barometer, manometer, inclined manometer, and differential manometer
Rotating fluids and accelerated rigid-body fluid motion as optional extensions
Forces on Submerged Surfaces
children.description: This subtopic turns pressure fields into resultant forces and locations of action.

children.title: Resultant hydrostatic force, center of pressure, centroid, and pressure prism
Plane surface, curved surface, horizontal component, and vertical component
Gates, tanks, sight glasses, vessel walls, and dam-like surfaces
Moment balance and line of action
Buoyancy and Stability
children.description: The goal is to analyze floating and submerged bodies.

children.title: Archimedes' principle, buoyant force, displaced volume, and apparent weight
Center of buoyancy, center of gravity, metacenter, and metacentric height
Floating stability, neutral buoyancy, and submerged body equilibrium
Hydrometers, separators, and settling objects

topics.title: Integral Conservation of Mass and Control-Volume Analysis
topics.description: Use control-volume thinking to model accumulation, inflow, outflow, and continuity.

children.title: Control Volumes and Continuity
children.description: Students learn to choose a boundary and account for mass crossing it.

children.title: System, control volume, control surface, and outward normal
Mass flow rate, volumetric flow rate, average velocity, and density variation
Steady continuity equation and incompressible continuity equation
Multiple inlet/outlet mixing, split streams, and recycle streams
Unsteady Mass Balances
children.description: This section connects fluid mechanics to filling, draining, and process transients.

children.title: Accumulation, inflow, outflow, generation term absence for total mass
Tank draining, filling tank, variable liquid level, and residence time
Quasi-steady assumption and lumped control volume
Compressible storage in gas tanks and line packing
Velocity Profiles and Average Quantities
children.description: The point is to connect local velocity fields to engineering flow rates.

children.title: Point velocity, area-average velocity, mass-average velocity, and bulk velocity
Velocity profile, flow area, wetted perimeter, and hydraulic diameter
Laminar parabolic profile and turbulent flatter profile
Correction factors for momentum and kinetic energy

topics.title: Integral Momentum Balances and Mechanical Energy
topics.description: Apply momentum balances and mechanical energy balances to flow systems and equipment.

children.title: Linear Momentum Balance
children.description: Students use Newton's second law for flowing fluids.

children.title: Momentum flux, pressure force, body force, wall shear force, and support force
Steady-flow momentum balance and unsteady momentum accumulation
Momentum correction factor beta
Bends, nozzles, jets, reducers, and vanes
Mechanical Energy Balance
children.description: This subtopic introduces the engineering energy equation for flow systems.

children.title: Pressure head, velocity head, elevation head, pump head, turbine head, and head loss
Shaft work, flow work, mechanical energy, and irreversible loss
Kinetic energy correction factor alpha
Extended Bernoulli equation and process piping examples
Forces and Equipment Loads
children.description: The goal is to compute loads that matter for design and support.

children.title: Reaction force, anchor force, thrust, impulse, and jet impact
Force on pipe elbow, nozzle thrust, and tank discharge force
Momentum balance with pressure and gravity terms
Free-body diagram and sign convention

topics.title: Bernoulli Equation, Energy Corrections, and Engineering Limits
topics.description: Use Bernoulli's equation appropriately while recognizing losses, pumps, turbines, and velocity profiles.

children.title: Bernoulli Equation Derivation and Assumptions
children.description: Students learn what Bernoulli's equation says and when it applies.

children.title: Inviscid flow, steady flow, incompressible flow, streamline, and no shaft work
Static pressure, dynamic pressure, stagnation pressure, and elevation term
Total head, piezometric head, and hydraulic grade line
Torricelli law, siphon, jet speed, and free-surface tank
Losses and Energy Additions
children.description: Real systems require corrections for pumps, turbines, and frictional loss.

children.title: Major loss, minor loss, loss coefficient K, and head-loss term
Pump head, turbine head, efficiency, and shaft power
Energy grade line and hydraulic grade line
Entrance loss, exit loss, valve loss, fitting loss, and contraction/expansion loss
Common Misuses and Validity Checks
children.description: The point is to avoid applying Bernoulli where viscous or rotational effects dominate.

children.title: Streamline restriction, separated flow, turbulence, and viscous dissipation
Compressibility effects and Mach-number caution
Nonuniform velocity profile and correction factors
Pressure taps, datum choice, and unit consistency

topics.title: Differential Momentum Transport and Navier-Stokes Equations
topics.description: Derive and interpret local momentum balances for Newtonian fluids.

children.title: Differential Balances and Field Variables
children.description: This subtopic moves from whole equipment balances to local equations.

children.title: Velocity field, pressure field, density field, and stress field
Material derivative, local acceleration, convective acceleration, and substantial derivative
Continuity equation in differential form
Cartesian, cylindrical, and spherical coordinate awareness
Stress Tensor and Newtonian Constitutive Law
children.description: Students learn how forces inside a fluid are represented mathematically.

children.title: Normal stress, shear stress, stress tensor, and pressure as isotropic normal stress
Rate-of-strain tensor, velocity gradient, and deformation rate
Newton's law of viscosity and Newtonian constitutive relation
Viscous stress, bulk viscosity, and Stokes hypothesis as an optional extension
Navier-Stokes Equations and Simplifications
children.description: The goal is to recognize which terms remain for common ChE flows.

children.title: Navier-Stokes equation, body force, pressure gradient, viscous diffusion, and inertia
Creeping flow, inviscid flow, fully developed flow, and unidirectional flow
Boundary condition: no slip, no penetration, symmetry, and free surface
Scale analysis and order-of-magnitude simplification

topics.title: Viscous Flow, Shear Stress, and Non-Newtonian Rheology
topics.description: Connect viscosity, shear stress, velocity gradients, and rheological models to transport behavior.

children.title: Shear Stress and Viscosity
children.description: Students connect velocity gradients to momentum diffusion and flow resistance.

children.title: Shear rate, shear stress, viscosity, and momentum diffusivity
Newtonian fluid, viscosity-temperature dependence, and viscosity-pressure dependence
Viscometer, capillary rheometer, and rotational rheometer
Wall shear stress and shear-stress distribution
Non-Newtonian Models
children.description: Many process fluids are not Newtonian, so students need the common model vocabulary.

children.title: Power-law fluid, consistency index, flow behavior index, and apparent viscosity
Bingham plastic, yield stress, Herschel-Bulkley model, and plug flow
Shear-thinning, shear-thickening, thixotropy, and viscoelasticity
Polymer solutions, slurries, paints, food products, and biological fluids
Viscous Flow Regimes
children.description: The point is to classify when viscosity dominates and how shear propagates momentum.

children.title: Reynolds number, creeping flow, laminar flow, transitional flow, and turbulent flow
Stokes flow, lubrication approximation, and thin-film flow
Entrance region, fully developed region, and wall effects
No-slip condition and wall-driven momentum transport

topics.title: Laminar Internal Flow and Exact Solutions
topics.description: Study fully developed laminar flows in simple geometries and their pressure-drop relationships.

children.title: Circular Pipe Flow
children.description: This subtopic develops the canonical pressure-driven laminar flow solution.

children.title: Hagen-Poiseuille equation, parabolic velocity profile, and volumetric flow rate
Wall shear stress, pressure gradient, and maximum/average velocity relation
Laminar friction factor 64/Re
Entrance length and fully developed laminar assumption
Planar and Annular Flows
children.description: Students learn how geometry changes exact solutions.

children.title: Plane Poiseuille flow, Couette flow, combined Couette-Poiseuille flow
Flow between parallel plates and moving wall problems
Annular flow, falling film, and slit flow
Boundary conditions, symmetry condition, and integration constants
Process Applications of Laminar Flow
children.description: The goal is to connect exact solutions to real process calculations.

children.title: Capillary flow, microfluidic channel, coating flow, and film flow
Residence time, shear exposure, and pressure-drop sizing
Laminar mixing limitations and diffusion-dominated transport
Scale-up cautions for viscosity-dominated systems

topics.title: Turbulence, Friction Factors, and Pipe-Flow Pressure Drop
topics.description: Model turbulent internal flow using empirical friction factors and engineering correlations.

children.title: Turbulent Flow Concepts
children.description: Students learn why turbulent flow requires empirical and statistical descriptions.

children.title: Velocity fluctuation, time-average velocity, Reynolds decomposition, and eddy
Turbulent mixing, eddy viscosity, and Reynolds stress
Laminar sublayer, buffer layer, logarithmic region, and turbulent core
Smooth pipe, rough pipe, and relative roughness
Friction Factor Methods
children.description: This subtopic builds the main pipe-flow calculation toolkit.

children.title: Darcy friction factor, Fanning friction factor, and conversion
Moody chart, Colebrook equation, Swamee-Jain equation, and explicit approximations
Reynolds number, relative roughness, and hydraulic diameter
Major head loss and Darcy-Weisbach equation
Minor Losses and Noncircular Ducts
children.description: The point is to include real fittings and geometry in pressure-drop estimates.

children.title: Minor-loss coefficient, entrance, exit, bend, elbow, tee, valve, and sudden expansion
Equivalent length method and K-value method
Hydraulic diameter, wetted perimeter, and noncircular duct correlation
Compressibility and high-velocity gas-flow caution

topics.title: Pumps, Compressors, Piping Networks, and Equipment Selection
topics.description: Analyze fluid-moving equipment, system curves, cavitation, and network behavior.

children.title: Pump Curves and System Curves
children.description: Students learn how fluid-moving equipment finds an operating point.

children.title: Centrifugal pump, positive displacement pump, pump curve, and system curve
Operating point, shutoff head, runout, and best efficiency point
Pump efficiency, brake horsepower, and affinity laws
Series pumps, parallel pumps, and variable-speed operation
Cavitation and NPSH
children.description: The goal is to prevent vapor formation and equipment damage.

children.title: Vapor pressure, cavitation, flashing, and suction pressure
Net positive suction head available and required
Suction line loss, elevation head, and temperature effects
Cavitation noise, impeller damage, and design margin
Piping Networks and Compressors
children.description: Students practice coupled equipment and network calculations.

children.title: Series pipe, parallel pipe, branch network, and equivalent resistance
Hardy Cross method preview and iterative balancing
Compressors, blowers, fans, pressure ratio, and gas density changes
Valve sizing, control valve pressure drop, and process safety considerations

topics.title: Flow Measurement and Experimental Fluid Mechanics
topics.description: Use pressure, velocity, and flow-rate measurement methods while accounting for calibration and uncertainty.

children.title: Pressure and Velocity Measurements
children.description: Students learn what instruments actually measure.

children.title: Static pressure tap, stagnation pressure, differential pressure, and manometer
Pitot tube, Pitot-static tube, hot-wire anemometer, and laser Doppler velocimetry
Pressure transducer, calibration curve, zero drift, and response time
Probe placement, disturbance, and alignment error
Flow-Rate Meters
children.description: This subtopic covers the common industrial flowmeter families.

children.title: Venturi meter, orifice plate, flow nozzle, and discharge coefficient
Rotameter, turbine meter, Coriolis meter, magnetic flowmeter, and ultrasonic flowmeter
Reynolds-number limits, permanent pressure loss, and meter rangeability
Calibration, installation length, and uncertainty
Experimental Uncertainty and Data Reduction
children.description: The point is to convert raw measurements into defensible flow results.

children.title: Measurement uncertainty, propagation of error, repeatability, and bias
Dimensional consistency, unit conversion, and data reconciliation
Curve fitting, empirical correlation, and residual analysis
Lab safety, pressure containment, and uncertainty reporting

topics.title: Dimensional Analysis, Similitude, and Transport Correlations
topics.description: Use nondimensional groups to scale experiments, organize correlations, and interpret transport regimes.

children.title: Buckingham Pi and Dimensionless Groups
children.description: Students learn to reduce variable lists and identify governing ratios.

children.title: Base dimensions, repeating variables, dimension matrix, and dimensionless product
Buckingham Pi theorem and rank of dimensional matrix
Reynolds number, Euler number, Froude number, Weber number, Mach number, and Strouhal number
Nusselt, Prandtl, Schmidt, Sherwood, and Stanton numbers as transport previews
Similarity and Scale Models
children.description: This subtopic explains how small models inform full-scale process systems.

children.title: Geometric similarity, kinematic similarity, and dynamic similarity
Model-prototype relation and scaling law
Reynolds similarity, Froude similarity, and competing similarity constraints
Wind tunnel, water tunnel, stirred tank scale-up, and packed-bed scale-up
Empirical Correlations
children.description: The goal is to use correlations responsibly within their valid range.

children.title: Correlation form, regression constant, exponent, and validity range
Friction-factor correlation, drag correlation, and pressure-drop correlation
Log-log plot, dimensional homogeneity, and uncertainty in correlations
Extrapolation risk and physical sanity checks

topics.title: Boundary Layers, External Flow, Drag, and Flow Around Objects
topics.description: Analyze viscous layers, separation, drag, lift, and flow over immersed bodies.

children.title: Boundary-Layer Concepts
children.description: Students learn why viscous effects concentrate near surfaces at high Reynolds number.

children.title: Boundary-layer thickness, displacement thickness, momentum thickness, and wall shear
Laminar boundary layer, turbulent boundary layer, and transition
Blasius solution, flat-plate skin friction, and local/average coefficients
Pressure gradient, adverse pressure gradient, and separation
Drag and Lift on Bodies
children.description: This subtopic connects flow patterns to forces on immersed objects.

children.title: Drag coefficient, lift coefficient, form drag, skin-friction drag, and pressure drag
Flow around sphere, cylinder, flat plate, and airfoil as examples
Wake, vortex shedding, Strouhal number, and separation point
Terminal velocity, settling velocity, and drag-regime correlations
Particles, Packed Beds, and Process Relevance
children.description: Chemical engineering uses external-flow ideas in particulate and porous systems.

children.title: Stokes law, creeping-flow drag, and correction factor
Particle Reynolds number, sphericity, and hindered settling
Packed bed, void fraction, Ergun equation, and pressure drop
Fluidization, minimum fluidization velocity, and entrainment preview

topics.title: Momentum Transport Analogies and Preparation for Heat/Mass Transfer
topics.description: Connect momentum transport to heat and mass transfer through flux laws, diffusivity, and dimensionless analogies.

children.title: Flux Laws and Diffusivity Analogy
children.description: Students learn the common mathematical structure behind transport modes.

children.title: Newton's law of viscosity, Fourier's law, and Fick's law
Momentum diffusivity, thermal diffusivity, and mass diffusivity
Flux, gradient, driving force, and transport coefficient
Molecular transport versus turbulent transport
Dimensionless Transport Analogies
children.description: This subtopic previews later heat and mass transfer courses using familiar momentum concepts.

children.title: Reynolds analogy, Prandtl analogy, Taylor analogy, and Chilton-Colburn analogy
Friction factor, Stanton number, Prandtl number, and Schmidt number
j-factor, heat-transfer coefficient, and mass-transfer coefficient
Limitations of analogies and role of turbulence
Integrated Transport Problem Solving
children.description: The final section helps students transfer momentum-balance habits into the rest of ChE transport.

children.title: Shell balance, control-volume balance, and differential balance as reusable templates
Boundary condition, constitutive equation, and driving force identification
Scaling analysis and dimensionless formulation
Preparation for conduction, convection, diffusion, mass transfer, and separations
